item.title: Intelligent and Trustworthy Web Information Systems
item.content:encoded:
Junhui Zhao, Beijing Jiaotong University

Jiaheng Wang, Southeast University

Hong Zhao, Tsinghua University

The Web ecosystem faces interconnected challenges to trust spanning technical vulnerabilities, content manipulation, and regulatory compliance. System-level attacks and data breaches are compounded by the ease with which generative AI enables mass production of false content. Simultaneously, regulations like the Digital Services Act and AI Act demand new levels of platform accountability and content moderation that conventional governance cannot support, creating an urgent need for integrated solutions.

This special issue seeks research on intelligent and trustworthy Web information systems addressing three interconnected themes: Web security, content integrity, and online discourse governance. The research should span six dimensions of trustworthiness including security, privacy, explainability, fairness, robustness and accountable human oversight. The call welcomes original research and review articles that integrate Web security techniques, content monitoring systems, AI-based detection methods, and platform governance approaches to build a trustworthy Web ecosystem.

item.title: Trust Under Disruption in B2B Relationships: Repair, Reciprocity, and Resilience in a Fragmenting World
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how trust functions in business-to-business relationships when confronted with significant disruptions and fragmentation. The focus encompasses the mechanisms through which organizations can repair damaged trust, the role of reciprocity in maintaining relationships under stress, and the capacity for resilience in unstable market environments.

item.title: The Challenges of Social Media Influencers: AI Integration, Strategic Agency, and New Business Models in Global-Local Digital Markets
item.content:encoded:
Raffaele Filieri, Audencia Business School

Elmira Djafarova, Northumbria University

Margot Racat, IDRAC Business School

Veronika Keller, Szechenyi Istvan University

Rickard Enstroem, MacEwan University

Social media influencer marketing faces uncertainty amid algorithm fatigue, regulatory scrutiny, declining consumer trust, and AI-generated influencers. Traditional theoretical frameworks struggle to explain how AI content, algorithmic curation, and synthetic personas reshape influence dynamics.

This special issue examines whether traditional influencer marketing is ending or undergoing paradigm shift in how influence is constructed, monetized, and governed. It explores how authenticity, artificial intelligence, and algorithmic mediation intersect to reshape influence practices while addressing emerging regulatory frameworks.

The issue welcomes empirically grounded contributions from multiple disciplines including strategy, media studies, consumer behavior, and technology management. It particularly encourages interdisciplinary, globally inclusive research examining non-Western contexts, emerging platforms, and underrepresented influencer communities.

Appel publié par Canadian Journal of Administrative Sciences / Revue Canadienne des Sciences de l Administration. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Trust, credibility, and authenticity in digital influence
  • Algorithmic mediation, platform governance, and market structure
  • Consumer resistance, fatigue, and agency
  • Virtual influencers, AI, and synthetic content
  • Cultural, generational, and global perspectives on influence
  • Professionalization, labor, and monetization in the creator economy
  • Ethics, power, and the dark side of influencer marketing
  • Expanding contexts of influence in B2B, nonprofit, and public sectors
  • Strategic navigation of platforms, algorithms, and AI tools across global-local digital markets
  • Authenticity and trust negotiation in activism, sustainability, and cause-related marketing

item.title: Trust, Authenticity, and Consumer Agency in AI-Mediated Omnichannel and Phygital Experiences
item.content:encoded:
Andrea Vocino, Deakin University

Marta Massi, Athabasca University

Sandro Castaldo, Bocconi University

AI is increasingly central to consumer-brand interactions across digital and physical channels, raising questions about how consumers form and maintain trust, evaluate brand authenticity, and retain agency in automated decision environments. This special issue seeks to understand the psychological mechanisms underlying consumer responses to AI-mediated marketing, particularly how trust develops across diverse touchpoints and human involvement levels.

Authenticity and consumer agency emerge as critical concerns when AI shapes brand communications and customer choices. As generative AI and personalization tools become more prevalent, consumers must evaluate whether experiences feel genuine and aligned with brand values, while simultaneously navigating questions of autonomy and control in algorithmically curated environments. The issue welcomes diverse methodological approaches to advance theory, measurement, and practical understanding of these interconnected phenomena.

Appel publié par Psychology and Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Trust formation, calibration, repair, and withdrawal in AI-mediated consumer-brand interactions across channels and touchpoints
  • Consumer judgments of authenticity in AI-generated content, recommendations, service encounters, and brand communications
  • Trust transfer between human employees, algorithmic agents, platforms, and brands in omnichannel and phygital journeys
  • Consumer agency, autonomy, control, and reactance in algorithmically curated or automated marketing environments
  • Psychological and design cues (e.g., disclosure, explainability, transparency, anthropomorphism) that affect trust and authenticity
  • Comparative consumer responses to human, AI, and hybrid service provision in retail, hospitality, health, education, and luxury contexts
  • Mechanisms of resistance, acceptance, and adaptation to AI across different risk levels, involvement levels, and product categories
  • Cross-cultural, generational, and demographic differences in responses to AI-mediated marketing and phygital experiences
  • Measurement development and validation for trust, authenticity, agency, and related constructs in AI-enabled consumer settings
  • Conceptual integrations linking consumer psychology, service systems, and digital platform research in AI-mediated markets

Timeline

  • January 31, 2027: Submission deadline
